history.summary: The Kalika Mata temple atop Pavagadh hill (about 762 m above sea level) is one of the Shakti Peethas — the symbolic toe of the goddess Sati is said to have fallen here — and the third of Gujarat's major Shakti Peethas, known for tantric worship. The small, plain temples set within fortifications have an open chowk in front with two altars for offerings; the chief ground-floor shrine holds three images (Kalika Mata at the centre, Mahakali to the right, Bahuchara Mata to the left), the inner image of the goddess being only the head (mukhwato) painted red, and the restored marble floor dates to about 1859 (a gift of the minister of Limbdi). Notably, the temple spire carries a Muslim shrine and mausoleum to Sadan Shah Pir, a Sufi saint, so the shrine is venerated by Hindu and Muslim devotees alike. The temple is described in the 15th-century drama Gangadas Pratap Vilasa Natakam; a popular legend tells of King Jaisinh of the Patai dynasty offending the Goddess and bringing the downfall of Champaner to Mahmud Begada's invasion. It is reached by a ~5 km jungle footpath (250 steps to the sanctum, per some accounts) or by the 740 m mono-cable ropeway from Manchi. Part of the Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site).

name: Kalika Mata Temple, Pavagadh
town_description: Pavagadh is a hill town in Panchmahal district, Gujarat, dominated by the 800-metre Pavagadh hill — one of India's oldest rock formations. Together with Champaner at its base, it forms the Champaner-Pavagadh Archaeological Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site where Hindu and Jain temples stand beside medieval Islamic mosques and palaces. It is a pilgrimage town centred on the hilltop Kalika Mata shrine, reached by a cable ropeway.
